text:
For a **long outage**, look for a portable power station around **2,000 Wh (2 kWh)**, with a **pure-sine-wave AC outlet** and enough continuous output for your heater and thermostat. That’s a useful starting point—not a guarantee of a particular runtime.

As a rough example, one sizing guide estimates a **24 W heat mat** might run about **6–8 hours from 288 Wh**, or roughly **two days from 2,073 Wh**. A **100 W ceramic heat emitter** on a thermostat averaging half power could use a 2,073 Wh station in about a day. Those are calculations, not measured runtimes; actual results depend on the heater’s duty cycle and the station’s losses. ([Sizing guide and assumptions](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-keep-reptile-heat-on-in-a-power-outage))

Before buying, check the wattage on your actual heater, and test the setup with the thermostat—don’t rely on the station’s advertised capacity alone. For a shorter outage, insulating the enclosure and having wrapped hand warmers or warm water bottles ready can help; Petco also advises using emergency heat sources and monitoring the animal. ([Petco outage guidance](https://www.petco.com/pet-education/reptile/general/caring-for-your-reptile-during-a-power-outage))

If you share your heater’s wattage and how many hours of backup you want, I can estimate the capacity you need more closely.
